commands.start: open mocks/index.html in a desktop browser

env.notes: No build toolchain; static assets only

guidance.scope: Applies to the entire repository rooted at this folder.
purpose: Provide fast orientation for agents and humans
Point to exact commands, paths, and configs
Capture decisions, tradeoffs, and open questions
Document current product focus on Succession Planning inside the Talent Management suite
guardrails: Do NOT create new mocks, screens, or sample data unless explicitly requested and specified by the Product Owner
Keep content static unless interactions are explicitly requested
Confirm scope and acceptance criteria before implementing any new screen or interaction
UI theme stays locked to light mode; remove any dark-mode toggles if reintroduced
Interactivity expectation is exactly the current experience (successor click opens modal, modal tabs toggle trend/latest); no new dynamic behavior without PO approval
quickStart: Primary machine-readable source is this file
Prefer declared commands over ad-hoc guesses
Ask before making destructive structural changes
Mock entry is mocks/index.html (hash routing works via file://)
mocksOverview: Static interactive mock lives under mocks/
No build step: open mocks/index.html directly in a browser
Active hash routes: /org (Succession Org Chart), /performance (Performance Evaluation placeholder), /cycle (Create Talent Planning Cycle placeholder)

summary: Executive org tree rooted at the CEO with VP-level branches; VP, Fleet Operations exposes a successor list with readiness chips

Org chart reflects the current hierarchy: Jordan Reyes (CEO) with Maya Chen, Elias Romero, Priya Nair, and Connor Blake reporting to Jordan; Olivia Brooks, Amir Hassan, and Lena Ortiz report up through Elias
Succession plan lives inside Elias Romero's node: three successor rows stay inline, use readiness color chips (green/yellow/red), and act as the only entry point to the Talent Card
Successor rows support keyboard and mouse activation, open the Talent Card modal, and expose placeholder action menu items

Assign Learning menu action opens a dedicated modal showing the selected employee plus Competency vs Catalog search tabs with searchable cards; selecting a card drills into a course detail modal with placeholder Assign CTA
Talent Card modal shows talent pool nominations, performance/potential nine-box (latest + trend toggle), rating trend chart, career goals, experience, skills, and education
Readiness chips map ready-green/yellow/red to Ready Now, 1-2 Years, and 3+ Years
Styling is light theme only with custom org connectors, modal layout, and SVG trend visuals
activeSuccessionMock.interactivity: Match existing behavior: click/keyboard to open modal, switch between Latest and Trend views inside modal.

structure: mocks/app.js — shell, header/sidebar, routes (only #/org) and nav highlighting
mocks/state.js — in-memory state with localStorage persistence retained for future scenarios
mocks/screens/orgchart.js — Succession Org Chart (only screen present; add new files only with PO approval)
addingScreens: Default experience must remain the Succession Org Chart
If approved, add mocks/screens/<name>.js, register it in mocks/app.js, and document the route here
environment: Target modern desktop browsers (Linux currently in use, but Windows/macOS acceptable)
No tooling versions beyond a browser
tasksNotes: Track current work in the tasks array of this file
agentNotes: Prefer minimal, targeted changes respecting existing structure
Do not introduce new dependencies without confirmation
Validate manually in the browser using the provided commands
mocks/index.html injects cache-busted CSS/JS URLs each load; keep the inline script so browsers do not cache updates

conventions.codeStyle: Keep edits small and consistent with existing plain JS/CSS; no repo-wide formatter

conventions.commitStyle: Confirm with Product Owner before branching or merging
